findings.issue: Wrong reading: the compound 挨拶代わり has rendaku and is read あいさつがわり (dictionary-listed, e.g. Daijisen あいさつがわり), not あいさつかわり.
findings.current: ほんのあいさつかわりです。
findings.suggested: ほんのあいさつがわりです。

findings.issue: In-context reading of 代わり inside the compound 挨拶代わり is がわり (rendaku, as in 身代わり・親代わり), not かわり.
Same rendaku error as kana: 挨拶代わり = aisatsugawari, not aisatsukawari.
Token list corrupted: two spurious tokens フランス and 語 are prepended before あなた, out of sentence order, duplicating the correctly placed フランス語 token later in the list; breaks token-sentence alignment.
findings.current: tokens[0]=フランス(ふらんす), tokens[1]=語(ご) placed before あなた
findings.suggested: Delete stray tokens[0] (フランス) and tokens[1] (語); フランス語 is already tokenized in its proper position.

findings.issue: Wrong referent stated twice: the one presumed dead is the implied 'he' (cf. en 'gave him up', lit_en '(he) was dead', expl_pt '(ele) estava morto'), not 彼ら, who are the ones giving up. expl_en says '(they) were dead'.
findings.current: 死んだ (died/dead) + ものだ forming 'that (they) were dead,'
findings.suggested: 死んだ (died/dead) + ものだ forming 'that (he) was dead'; likewise 'on the assumption that he was dead'

findings.issue: Spurious modal: やってくるのですか contains no obligation; it asks whether they are coming too. 'Should come' changes the sense of the literal mirror (would correspond to 来るべき).
findings.current: They too should come (te-form + come), is that the case?
findings.suggested: They too come along (te-form + come), is that the case?

findings.issue: 'As for...' is the course's literal-mirror device for the topic particle は, but 布団 is marked by を (direct object); the literal mirror mis-signals the particle structure (expl correctly calls 布団を the object).
findings.current: As for the futon, put it away (command with なさい).
findings.suggested: The futon — put (it) away (command with なさい).

findings.issue: 'Quanto a...' is the course's mirror for は-topics, but 布団 is を-marked (direct object); the literal wrongly signals a topic where there is an object.
findings.current: Quanto ao futon, guarde-o (ordem com なさい).
findings.suggested: O futon, guarde(-o) (ordem com なさい).

findings.issue: ベル is the subject of 鳴る inside the relative clause (ベルの鳴る = ベルが鳴る, ga-no conversion), not a mere modifier; the parallel sentence ふりがなのある correctly labels the の-marked noun 'sujeito da oração modificadora'.
findings.suggested: sujeito da oração relativa (の no lugar de が)

findings.issue: やって is called 'auxiliary of やってくる', contradicting expl_en/expl_pt which call やる the main verb; in Japanese the auxiliary is the second verb (くる), never the te-form first element. Same wording in tokens[3].pt ('aqui auxiliar').
findings.current: to do (here auxiliary of やってくる: 'to come along')
findings.suggested: to do (first element of the compound やってくる: 'to come along')

findings.issue: In this sentence 腕を組む means linking arms with each other ('arm in arm', per en/pt), not folding one's own arms; 'fold (one's arms)' glosses the other sense. The pt gloss ('entrelaçar') already covers the right one.
findings.suggested: to link, to lock (arms with someone)

findings.issue: Ga-no conversion in noun-modifying clauses is standard Japanese (if anything slightly formal/literary); calling の a 'colloquial substitute' teaches a wrong register fact.
findings.current: here の is a colloquial substitute for が inside the modifying clause
findings.suggested: here の substitutes が inside the modifying clause (a standard alternative in noun-modifying clauses)

findings.issue: Same wrong register claim as expl_en: の replacing が in modifying clauses is standard, not 'coloquial'.
findings.current: aqui o の é um substituto coloquial de が dentro da oração modificadora
findings.suggested: aqui o の substitui が dentro da oração modificadora (alternativa padrão em orações modificadoras)
